summary: The agent passed all baseline tests but failed 6 of 137 new integrity-maintenance tests due to incorrect symlink, shared-file, and hard-link handling.

details.reasoning: The implementation is substantial and compiles, but its filesystem identity model is incomplete. forgetRule() deletes entry.target, which is the symlink target, without also deleting the recorded symlink. inspect() tracks recorded names textually and only marks entries shared when both resolved targets are valid, so aliases to an in-folder file are reported as unowned and aliases to an outside file are discarded instead of remaining shared. Save-time cleanup also rejects an outside entry even when another entry shares it, instead of removing only the requested index entry. Finally, writableTarget() compares paths rather than file identity for an existing hard link to stored.rules, allowing a save to overwrite the index. These defects account for all six reported failures.

quick_failure_summary: Six new tests fail because symlink aliases and hard links are not handled by the required ownership, sharing, deletion, and index-protection rules.

justification.issue_description: The solution does not preserve file identity semantics for symlink and hard-link entries: it leaves dangling links after deletion, reports linked targets as unowned, fails to recognize outside-file aliases as shared, rejects the required outside shared-entry cleanup, and can write through a hard link to stored.rules.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly requires that two entries resolving to one file are shared, that an entry naming a link owns its target, that resolved repair deletes the link together with its target, that outside content is never touched, and that storing never writes over the index. In the patch, inspect() uses recordedNames.contains(child.getFileName().toString()) and only compares sameFile() when both entries are valid, while forgetRule() calls Files.deleteIfExists(entry.target) without deleting entry.lexicalPath. The verifier reports failures in forgettingARuleWhoseEntryNamesALinkToAFileNoOtherEntryRecordsDiscardsLinkAndFile, aResolvedEntryNamingALinkDiscardsTheFileTheLinkPointsAt, anEntryNamingALinkToAFileInTheStoreOwnsThatFile, twoEntriesReachingOneFileByDifferentNamesShareItAndNeitherIsDiscarded, forgettingARuleWhoseNameEscapesTheFolderNeverTouchesAnythingOutside, and storingARuleWhoseEntryRecordsAnotherPathToTheIndexIsRejected.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is an agent coding failure rather than an undocumented expectation: each missed behavior is stated directly in the task. The implementation runs and passes the baseline suite, but its classification and save algorithms do not implement the explicit link/identity rules, so FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is the appropriate primary verdict.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is difficult but solvable and specifies the relevant symlink, hard-link, path-safety, repair, and concurrency semantics. The reference implementation and test run provide no indication of a broken or nondeterministic verifier.

evidence: test_execution.log reports a successful baseline run of 42/42 tests and a new-test run of 131/137 with six ordinary assertion or store-exception failures.
junit_base.xml has zero failures and junit_new.xml has six failures, all originating from TextFileBasedViolationStore behavior rather than test bootstrap or dependency setup.

The trajectory shows successful production compilation and focused legacy/concurrency verification; there is no observed dependency, permission, runtime, or service failure that diverted the implementation.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external environment or verifier blocker was found; the remaining failures are attributable to the implementation.
